notes: Lanes say where we look; requirements say what a signal means, and the two are never merged. Each lane sits under one of the three lenses the commission asked for: government, partnership and wider society, and international.

lanes.name: Welsh Government
lanes.description: Welsh Government policy, legislation, consultations, statistics and the remit letter to Natural Resources Wales (NRW).

lanes.name: Senedd
lanes.description: Senedd Cymru business: committee inquiries and reports, plenary questions, Bills and research briefings.

lanes.name: UK Government and regulators
lanes.description: UK Government departments, UK-wide regulators and advisory bodies whose decisions reach Wales.

lanes.name: Research and evidence
lanes.description: Peer-reviewed research, research councils and evidence centres publishing findings relevant to the Welsh environment.

lanes.name: Partnership and civil society
lanes.description: Partners, farming unions, environmental charities, public services boards and utilities working with or alongside NRW.

lanes.name: Legal and campaign
lanes.description: Campaign groups and legal challenges that test regulators and policy, including judicial reviews and complaints.

lanes.name: Independent media
lanes.description: News and investigative journalism reporting on the Welsh environment and the bodies that manage it.

lanes.name: Ecological surveillance
lanes.description: Statutory and scientific surveillance schemes that give early warning of disease, invasive species, drought and other biophysical change.

lanes.name: International
lanes.description: United Nations, European Union and other international bodies, conventions and Conferences of the Parties (COPs) whose approaches bear on Wales.

lanes.name: Governance and capacity
lanes.description: Audit, scrutiny and watchdog bodies reporting on the funding, governance and delivery capacity of Welsh public bodies.
